func IncrementRequeueStatus(sid string) int {
	prefix := os.Getenv("PREFIX")
	key := fmt.Sprintf("%s_requeue_status:%s", prefix, sid)

issues.display_title: Issue #489: API Logout GoThru SSO
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Guide: Keycloak SSO Logout & Universal Logout API

  • Related Issue: GoThruMedia/panorra-api-new#489
  • Target Service: panorra-api-go-new
  • Endpoints: POST /auth/keycloak/logout and POST /auth/logout
  • Status: Implemented & Verified

1. Overview & Purpose

When a user logs in through GoThru Keycloak Single Sign-On (SSO), a session is created both within Keycloak and within Panorra (stored as a local JWT token).

If the frontend (FE) only deletes the Panorra token from the browser storage (e.g., localStorage), the Keycloak SSO session remains active. This causes issues such as:

  1. When the user returns to login, Keycloak still considers them authenticated and logs them back in automatically without asking for credentials.
  2. The Keycloak refresh_token remains valid and could be abused.
  3. The local Panorra user profile remains cached in Redis until expiration.
  4. No logout audit trail is recorded.

To resolve this, the API provides two coordinated endpoints:

  • POST /auth/keycloak/logout: Dedicated Keycloak SSO logout endpoint for applications explicitly handling SSO tokens.
  • POST /auth/logout: Universal logout endpoint that handles all authentication methods (Keycloak SSO, Email/Password, Google, and Apple) through a single unified route.
